name: Agomelatine
lead: Agomelatine is an antidepressant developed by Servier and sold as Valdoxan. It is an agonist at melatonin MT1 and MT2 receptors and an antagonist at serotonin 5-HT2C receptors [1][2][3]. It was authorised in the European Union in 2009 and is available in several other countries, but it has not been approved by the US FDA [1].

It is listed in the wiki's recovery category because of its sleep-related, melatonin-linked mechanism. No study has examined it for appearance, and no looksmaxxing community discussion of it was identified.
Network meta-analysis of antidepressants has compared it with other agents for major depression [4]. Liver monitoring is part of its use because of reports of raised liver enzymes [1].

paras: Agomelatine is authorised in the EU for major depressive episodes in adults [1]. Anxiety disorders have also been studied, and the registered trials listed below include depression with comorbid conditions such as fibromyalgia and schizophrenia [5][6].

Reported common effects include headache, nausea, dizziness, somnolence and fatigue, typically early in treatment [1]. Reviews describe a low rate of sexual dysfunction relative to many antidepressants [1][7]. Raised liver transaminases are reported in a minority of users, and prescribing information calls for liver function testing; the drug is contraindicated in hepatic impairment and with potent CYP1A2 inhibitors such as fluvoxamine [1].

Agomelatine's antidepressant action is attributed to combined MT1/MT2 agonism and 5-HT2C antagonism, the latter shown in preclinical work to enhance frontocortical dopaminergic and noradrenergic activity [3][8]. A 2010 review in Nature Reviews Drug Discovery describes its discovery and development as the first melatonergic antidepressant [9].

Phase 3 placebo-controlled trials in major depression include NCT00411242 (503 participants) and trials of a sublingual formulation [10][11]. The 2018 Lancet network meta-analysis of 21 antidepressants compared agomelatine with other drugs for acute treatment of adult depression [4]. Smaller registered trials examined cardiovascular effects, augmentation, depression in schizophrenia and post-stroke depression prevention [6][12]. No studies were found on agomelatine for appearance outcomes.

card.summary: A melatonin-linked antidepressant sold in Europe, not the US; no appearance evidence.
card.note: Liver enzyme monitoring is part of prescribing; not FDA approved.

quick.overview:
Agomelatine is a prescription antidepressant authorised in the EU and some other countries but not in the US. It acts on melatonin receptors as well as a serotonin receptor.

No studies tie it to appearance, and it appears here because of its sleep and circadian angle.
quick.mechanism: It activates MT1 and MT2 melatonin receptors and blocks 5-HT2C receptors, which preclinical work links to increased dopamine and noradrenaline in the frontal cortex.
quick.risks: Reported effects include headache, nausea, dizziness and sleepiness. Raised liver enzymes have been reported, so liver testing is part of use, and it is contraindicated in hepatic impairment.
